summary: This part of the Privacy Enhanced Mail series defines the cryptographic algorithms, usage modes, and identifiers used to support PEM, with formats and references. It is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC specifies cryptographic algorithms and the exact names and formats used by Privacy Enhanced Mail (PEM). It is now Historic and describes an earlier email security system.

questions: algorithms used in privacy enhanced mail
what is pem privacy enhanced mail
subtitle: The algorithms, modes, identifiers, and parameters specified for Privacy Enhanced Mail.

tldr.problem: PEM needed precise names and formats for the cryptographic algorithms used to encrypt and authenticate mail.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC specifies message encryption, integrity checks, symmetric and asymmetric key management, and identifiers used in PEM headers.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1423 is Historic and obsoleted RFC 1115; it was part of the multi-document PEM series.

today: RFC 1423 is Historic and obsoleted RFC 1115. It was published as Part III of the PEM series, alongside RFC 1421, RFC 1422, and RFC 1424.

sections.title: What This Part of PEM Defines
sections.content:
RFC 1423 is Part III of the Privacy Enhanced Mail (PEM) documents. It defines algorithms, usage modes, identifiers, and parameters for PEM, separated from the other PEM procedures so that algorithm details could be changed independently.

The document covers message encryption, message integrity checks, symmetric key management, and asymmetric key management. It replaces RFC 1115.
sections.plainLanguage: This part of PEM is a catalog of cryptographic methods and their identifiers. It is separate from the documents that describe the rest of the mail procedures.

sections.title: Message Encryption with DES-CBC
sections.content:
The RFC defines DES in Cipher Block Chaining mode as its message-encryption algorithm. The header identifier is DES-CBC. Before encryption, the message is padded to a multiple of 8 octets, and each encrypted message uses a new pseudorandom key and initialization vector.

The key is 64 bits, including 8 parity bits, and the initialization vector is 64 bits. A DEK-Info: header carries the algorithm name and the vector as 16 hexadecimal digits.
sections.plainLanguage: PEM uses DES-CBC to encrypt message text. The sender includes a fresh starting value in the header so the receiver can decrypt the message.

sections.title: Message Integrity Checks
sections.content:
A Message Integrity Check (MIC) is a digest used to detect changes to a message. RFC 1423 defines RSA-MD2 and RSA-MD5, each producing a 16-octet digest and having an ASN.1 object identifier.

A compliant implementation must be able to process both algorithms on incoming messages. The sender chooses which one to use for an outgoing message. With symmetric key management, the digest is split into two parts and encrypted separately.
sections.plainLanguage: A MIC is a short digest of a message. The receiver can compare it with a newly calculated digest to detect changes.

sections.title: Symmetric and Asymmetric Key Management
sections.content:
For symmetric key management, PEM specifies DES-ECB as required support and DES-EDE as an optional mode for encrypting data-encryption keys and MIC values. For asymmetric key management, the RFC specifies RSA public keys and RSAEncryption.

The RSA public exponent must be 65537 or 3, and the modulus may range from 508 to 1024 bits. The RFC defines how encrypted keys and MICs are padded and represented, and how RSA-MD2 is used to sign certificates and certificate revocation lists.
sections.plainLanguage: PEM can protect keys with a shared secret or with RSA public-key encryption. The RFC gives exact rules for the required identifiers and data formats.

sections.title: Identifiers, Security, and Patent Note
sections.content:
The descriptive grammar lists the names used in PEM headers, including DES-CBC, DES-ECB, DES-EDE, RSA, RSA-MD2, and RSA-MD5. It also specifies formats for initialization vectors and encrypted values.

The Security Considerations section says that the entire document is about security. A separate patent statement describes the public-key patents and licensing assurance cited when the RFC was published.
sections.plainLanguage: The final grammar makes the identifiers and their formats explicit. The RFC also records the patent statement that accompanied this version of PEM.
